paragraphs.title: The Altar of Incense and Its Incense

easy.question: What was the incense altar made of?
answers: Shittim wood
Marble
Bronze only
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that the incense altar was to be made of shittim wood.

easy.question: What material covered the incense altar?
answers: Silver
Pure gold
Blue cloth
easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold.”

easy.question: Who was commanded to burn incense on the altar?
answers: Moses
Bezaleel
Aaron
easy.explanation: Verses 7–8 say that Aaron was to burn the incense.

medium.question: When was Aaron to burn the incense?
answers: In the morning and at evening
Only once a week
Only on New Year’s Day
medium.explanation: The incense was burned in the morning when the lamps were trimmed and again in the evening when they were lit.

medium.question: What does “strange incense” mean in the command, “Ye shall offer no strange incense thereon”?
answers: Incense not authorized or suitable for the altar
Incense made of gold
Incense burned in the morning
medium.explanation: “Strange incense” means incense not authorized for the altar; the verse also forbids burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings there.

medium.question: Why did the altar have rings and staves?
answers: To hang lamps on it
To carry it from place to place
To measure its height
medium.explanation: Verse 4 says the rings were for the staves used to carry the altar.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that incense was burned both morning and evening?
answers: The service was regular and daily
Incense was permitted only on the Sabbath
The altar was used only during journeys
challenge.explanation: Mentioning two times each day shows that burning incense was a regular, continual service throughout the generations.

challenge.question: Where was the incense altar placed?
answers: Outside the tabernacle courtyard
Before the veil, opposite the ark of the testimony
Inside the ark of the testimony
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 says it was to be placed before the veil, near the ark of the testimony.

challenge.question: What was distinctive about the atonement made on the horns of the incense altar?
answers: It was made once a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonement
It was made every morning with oil
It was made only when the tabernacle was built
challenge.explanation: Verse 10 says Aaron was to make atonement on the altar’s horns once a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonement.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that incense was burned both morning and evening?
answers: The service was regular and daily
Incense was permitted only on the Sabbath
The altar was used only during journeys
questions.explanation: Mentioning two times each day shows that burning incense was a regular, continual service throughout the generations.

questions.question: Where was the incense altar placed?
answers: Outside the tabernacle courtyard
Before the veil, opposite the ark of the testimony
Inside the ark of the testimony
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says it was to be placed before the veil, near the ark of the testimony.

questions.question: What was distinctive about the atonement made on the horns of the incense altar?
answers: It was made once a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonement
It was made every morning with oil
It was made only when the tabernacle was built
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says Aaron was to make atonement on the altar’s horns once a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonement.

paragraphs.title: The Half-Shekel for the Census of Israel

easy.question: Who spoke the commands in these verses to Moses?
answers: Pharaoh
The LORD
Aaron
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “And the LORD spake unto Moses.”

easy.question: How much was each person counted in the census to give?
answers: Half a shekel
A full shekel
Ten gerahs
easy.explanation: Each person counted was to give half a shekel.

easy.question: At what age did a person become required to give the LORD’s offering?
answers: Twenty years old
Thirty years old
Ten years old
easy.explanation: The verse says, “from twenty years old and above.”

medium.question: Why was each person required to give a ransom during the census?
answers: So that no plague would come upon them
To buy food
To choose a leader
medium.explanation: The verse connects the payment with preventing a plague when the people were counted.

medium.question: What does the phrase “among them that are numbered” refer to?
answers: Those traveling with them
Those counted in the census
Their commanders
medium.explanation: The context concerns numbering and counting the children of Israel, so the phrase refers to those counted.

medium.question: What was done with the atonement money collected from the Israelites?
answers: It was distributed to the poor
It was kept by Moses
It was appointed for the service of the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The verse commands that the money be appointed for the service of the tabernacle.

challenge.question: What social principle is emphasized by saying that the rich should not give more and the poor should not give less?
answers: Everyone contributes the same amount
The rich are exempt from payment
The poor give according to their means
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that everyone gives the same half-shekel, regardless of wealth.

challenge.question: What was the purpose of the money beyond being a payment?
answers: To trade with other nations
To be a memorial before the LORD and make atonement for their souls
To serve as Moses’ wages
challenge.explanation: The money was an atonement offering and a memorial before the LORD for the Israelites.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the requirement applying to everyone counted from age twenty onward?
answers: The offering was given only by family heads
The offering was given only by priests
The obligation was connected with membership in the adult census of the nation
challenge.explanation: The verses connect the offering with the census and define those required to give as those aged twenty and over who were counted.

questions.question: What social principle is emphasized by saying that the rich should not give more and the poor should not give less?
answers: Everyone contributes the same amount
The rich are exempt from payment
The poor give according to their means
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that everyone gives the same half-shekel, regardless of wealth.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the money beyond being a payment?
answers: To trade with other nations
To be a memorial before the LORD and make atonement for their souls
To serve as Moses’ wages
questions.explanation: The money was an atonement offering and a memorial before the LORD for the Israelites.

questions.question: What can we infer from the requirement applying to everyone counted from age twenty onward?
answers: The offering was given only by family heads
The offering was given only by priests
The obligation was connected with membership in the adult census of the nation
questions.explanation: The verses connect the offering with the census and define those required to give as those aged twenty and over who were counted.

paragraphs.title: The Brass Laver and the Washing of the Priests

easy.question: What was the laver made of?
answers: Brass
Gold
Wood
easy.explanation: The verse calls it a “laver of brass.”

easy.question: Who washed their hands and feet at the laver?
answers: All the Israelites
Aaron and his sons
Moses alone
easy.explanation: The verse specifically says that Aaron and his sons washed their hands and feet there.

easy.question: What was placed in the laver?
answers: Oil
Blood
Water
easy.explanation: The verse says, “thou shalt put water therein.”

medium.question: Why did the priests have to wash before serving?
answers: So that they would not die
So that the laver would remain full
So that they could leave the camp
medium.explanation: The verses repeat the warning, “that they die not.”

medium.question: What was the purpose of the laver’s brass base?
answers: It held the water inside the laver
It served as the laver’s stand or support
It covered the laver
medium.explanation: The verse mentions the laver and its base separately, indicating that the base supported the laver.

medium.question: When were Aaron and his sons required to wash?
answers: When entering the tabernacle or approaching the altar to minister
Only after finishing their service
Only when it rained
medium.explanation: The verse names two occasions: entering the tabernacle and approaching the altar to minister.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the laver’s position between the tabernacle and the altar?
answers: It stored the tabernacle vessels
It stood outside the camp
The priests washed there before entering into holy service
challenge.explanation: Its position between the tabernacle and the altar fits its role as a place of washing before priestly service.

challenge.question: What does the repeated command to wash emphasize?
answers: Washing was a regular and essential requirement
The priests washed only their feet
The water was changed every day
challenge.explanation: The repeated command and warning that they would die emphasize that washing was a regular and essential requirement.

challenge.question: For whom was this command intended according to “to him and to his seed throughout their generations”?
answers: Every Israelite in every situation
Aaron and his descendants throughout the generations
Moses and the elders alone
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the command applied to Aaron and his descendants—the priests—throughout the generations.

questions.question: What can we infer from the laver’s position between the tabernacle and the altar?
answers: It stored the tabernacle vessels
It stood outside the camp
The priests washed there before entering into holy service
questions.explanation: Its position between the tabernacle and the altar fits its role as a place of washing before priestly service.

questions.question: What does the repeated command to wash emphasize?
answers: Washing was a regular and essential requirement
The priests washed only their feet
The water was changed every day
questions.explanation: The repeated command and warning that they would die emphasize that washing was a regular and essential requirement.

questions.question: For whom was this command intended according to “to him and to his seed throughout their generations”?
answers: Every Israelite in every situation
Aaron and his descendants throughout the generations
Moses and the elders alone
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the command applied to Aaron and his descendants—the priests—throughout the generations.

easy.question: To whom did the LORD speak at the beginning of this passage?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “the LORD spake unto Moses.”

easy.question: What kind of oil was required for the anointing oil?
answers: Sesame oil
Olive oil
Fish oil
easy.explanation: Verse 24 explicitly calls for olive oil, an hin.

easy.question: What was to be made from the spices and oil?
answers: Incense
Medicine
Holy anointing oil
easy.explanation: Verse 25 says, “it shall be an holy anointing oil.”

medium.question: Which ingredient was listed in an amount of five hundred shekels?
answers: Pure myrrh
Sweet cinnamon
Sweet calamus
medium.explanation: Pure myrrh was listed at five hundred shekels, while cinnamon and calamus were each listed at two hundred fifty.

medium.question: What does the phrase “after the art of the apothecary” indicate?
answers: It was made by someone who sold clothing
It was prepared by someone skilled in making aromatic mixtures
It was made by someone who guarded the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a person skilled in preparing aromatic compounds.

medium.question: What was done after the spices and olive oil were gathered?
answers: They were thrown away
They were distributed among the people
They were compounded into holy anointing oil
medium.explanation: After listing the ingredients, the passage says they were to be compounded into holy anointing oil.

challenge.question: Which ingredient was listed at half of five hundred shekels?
answers: Sweet cinnamon
Pure myrrh
Cassia
challenge.explanation: Cinnamon was listed as half the amount of five hundred shekels—two hundred fifty.

challenge.question: What does “an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary” teach about preparing the oil?
answers: The oil was made without mixing
Its preparation required skilled compounding
The oil was intended only as household perfume
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the oil was a carefully prepared mixture requiring professional skill.

challenge.question: What distinguishes the olive oil from the spices in the list of measurements?
answers: It was measured by an hin rather than by sanctuary shekels
It was measured at five hundred shekels
It was not part of the preparation
challenge.explanation: The spices were measured in shekels, while the olive oil was measured by the volume measure called an hin.

questions.question: Which ingredient was listed at half of five hundred shekels?
answers: Sweet cinnamon
Pure myrrh
Cassia
questions.explanation: Cinnamon was listed as half the amount of five hundred shekels—two hundred fifty.

questions.question: What does “an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary” teach about preparing the oil?
answers: The oil was made without mixing
Its preparation required skilled compounding
The oil was intended only as household perfume
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the oil was a carefully prepared mixture requiring professional skill.

questions.question: What distinguishes the olive oil from the spices in the list of measurements?
answers: It was measured by an hin rather than by sanctuary shekels
It was measured at five hundred shekels
It was not part of the preparation
questions.explanation: The spices were measured in shekels, while the olive oil was measured by the volume measure called an hin.

easy.question: What was done to the tabernacle and the ark of the testimony?
answers: They were anointed with oil
They were burned
They were kept outside the camp
easy.explanation: Verse 26 says, “thou shalt anoint the tabernacle of the congregation therewith, and the ark of the testimony.”

easy.question: Which of the following is mentioned in these verses?
answers: The courtyard
The candlestick
The clothing
easy.explanation: The candlestick and its vessels are mentioned in verse 27.

easy.question: What happens to whatever touches the vessels after they are sanctified?
answers: It becomes unclean
It must move away
It becomes holy
easy.explanation: The end of verse 29 says, “whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy.”

medium.question: What sequence is described for the holy vessels?
answers: They are first anointed and then sanctified
They are first sanctified and then burned
They are first dismantled and then anointed
medium.explanation: The passage first says, “thou shalt anoint,” and then says, “thou shalt sanctify them.”

medium.question: What do the items listed in verses 26–28 have in common?
answers: They are all weapons
They are all connected with holy worship
They are all outside the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The tabernacle, ark, table, candlestick, altars, and laver were all part of the place and service of worship.

medium.question: What was the function of the laver’s base?
answers: It held the water inside the laver
It covered the laver
It supported the laver
medium.explanation: The laver and its base are mentioned separately, indicating that the base supported it.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the mention of the vessels of the table, candlestick, and altars?
answers: The vessels connected with holy service were also included in the sanctification
Only the vessels mattered, not the larger objects
The vessels were intended for ordinary use
challenge.explanation: The verses emphasize that not only the main objects but also their vessels were anointed and sanctified.

challenge.question: What does “whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy” mean?
answers: Anyone who touches them must move away
Whatever touches them becomes holy
Only a priest may look at them
challenge.explanation: The statement explicitly says that whatever touches the sanctified objects becomes holy.

challenge.question: What does the expression “most holy” emphasize about the anointed objects?
answers: They were holy only at certain times
They belonged equally to everyone
They had an especially high degree of holiness
challenge.explanation: “Most holy” expresses an especially high and distinctive degree of holiness.

questions.question: What can we infer from the mention of the vessels of the table, candlestick, and altars?
answers: The vessels connected with holy service were also included in the sanctification
Only the vessels mattered, not the larger objects
The vessels were intended for ordinary use
questions.explanation: The verses emphasize that not only the main objects but also their vessels were anointed and sanctified.

questions.question: What does “whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy” mean?
answers: Anyone who touches them must move away
Whatever touches them becomes holy
Only a priest may look at them
questions.explanation: The statement explicitly says that whatever touches the sanctified objects becomes holy.

questions.question: What does the expression “most holy” emphasize about the anointed objects?
answers: They were holy only at certain times
They belonged equally to everyone
They had an especially high degree of holiness
questions.explanation: “Most holy” expresses an especially high and distinctive degree of holiness.

paragraphs.title: Anointing Aaron and His Sons for the Priesthood

easy.question: Whom does the verse command to be anointed?
answers: Aaron and his sons
Moses alone
All the people
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “thou shalt anoint Aaron and his sons.”

easy.question: Why were Aaron and his sons consecrated?
answers: To become kings
To minister to the LORD as priests
To go to war
easy.explanation: They were consecrated so that they could minister to the LORD in the priest’s office.

easy.question: What is the first action mentioned in the verse?
answers: Sanctifying
Serving as priests
Anointing
easy.explanation: The verse first says they were to be anointed, and then consecrated.

medium.question: What is the relationship between anointing and priestly service in the verse?
answers: Anointing and consecration prepare Aaron and his sons for priestly service
Anointing removes them from the priesthood
Anointing occurs only after they finish serving
medium.explanation: The verse links anointing and consecration with preparing them to serve as priests.

medium.question: What does “thou shalt anoint Aaron and his sons” mean?
answers: You shall clothe them
You shall apply oil to them and set them apart for service
You shall send them elsewhere
medium.explanation: To anoint them means to apply oil in a consecration ceremony, setting them apart for priestly service.

medium.question: What does the order of the actions teach?
answers: They serve first and are anointed afterward
Anointing and consecration are unrelated
They are first anointed, then consecrated, and then appointed for priestly service
medium.explanation: The verse presents a sequence of anointing, consecration, and preparation for priestly service.

challenge.question: To whom does “them” refer in “thou shalt consecrate them”?
answers: Aaron and his sons together
The Israelites alone
Moses and Aaron only
challenge.explanation: “Them” refers back to Aaron and his sons, who were named at the beginning of the verse.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the words “that they may minister unto me”?
answers: They would serve themselves
Their priestly service was dedicated to the LORD
They would serve only once
challenge.explanation: The words “unto me” show that their priestly service was dedicated to the LORD.

challenge.question: Why are both Aaron and his sons mentioned?
answers: To teach that only Aaron was chosen
To teach that his sons had no connection with holy service
To show that the consecration included Aaron and his descendants
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly includes Aaron and his sons, showing that the consecration applied to the whole priestly family.

questions.question: To whom does “them” refer in “thou shalt consecrate them”?
answers: Aaron and his sons together
The Israelites alone
Moses and Aaron only
questions.explanation: “Them” refers back to Aaron and his sons, who were named at the beginning of the verse.

questions.question: What can we infer from the words “that they may minister unto me”?
answers: They would serve themselves
Their priestly service was dedicated to the LORD
They would serve only once
questions.explanation: The words “unto me” show that their priestly service was dedicated to the LORD.

questions.question: Why are both Aaron and his sons mentioned?
answers: To teach that only Aaron was chosen
To teach that his sons had no connection with holy service
To show that the consecration included Aaron and his descendants
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly includes Aaron and his sons, showing that the consecration applied to the whole priestly family.

paragraphs.title: The Anointing Oil Is Holy for the Generations

easy.question: What is described in these verses?
answers: Holy anointing oil
Special incense
Holy water
easy.explanation: The verses describe holy anointing oil belonging to the LORD.

easy.question: To whom did the anointing oil belong, and for how long?
answers: To Moses alone for one day
To the LORD throughout Israel’s generations
To the priests for one year
easy.explanation: The verse says it is holy to the LORD throughout the generations.

easy.question: What was the punishment for anyone who compounded oil like the anointing oil?
answers: He had to bring an offering
He received a fine
He was cut off from his people
easy.explanation: The verse says that anyone who compounded oil like it would be cut off from his people.

medium.question: Why was it forbidden to make oil according to the same formula?
answers: Because it was holy
Because it was very expensive
Because it had no fragrance
medium.explanation: The verse says, “it is holy, and it shall be holy unto you,” so it could not be prepared for ordinary use.

medium.question: What does “according to the composition of it” refer to?
answers: The place where it was kept
Its ingredients or formula
The time when it was used
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the oil’s particular composition or formula, which others were forbidden to copy.

medium.question: What two prohibitions appear in these verses?
answers: It was forbidden to keep the oil or smell it
It was forbidden to use the oil or give it to priests
It was forbidden to make such oil and to put it on a stranger
medium.explanation: The verses forbid both making oil like the anointing oil and putting it on a stranger.

challenge.question: What can we infer from “holy to me throughout your generations” together with “it shall be holy unto you”?
answers: The oil’s holiness was lasting, and it belonged to the LORD throughout the generations
Anyone could make it whenever convenient
It was intended only for the generation that left Egypt
challenge.explanation: Together these statements show that the oil was holy and remained associated with the LORD in future generations.

challenge.question: What does “Upon man’s flesh shall it not be poured” add to the prohibition against putting it on a stranger?
answers: It was permitted only for cooking
It could not be used for ordinary personal purposes or on someone unauthorized
It could be applied to every Israelite
challenge.explanation: The verse rules out ordinary use on a person’s body and specifically forbids putting it on a stranger.

challenge.question: Who received the punishment of being cut off?
answers: Only the person who received the oil
Only the person who stored the oil
Both the person who compounded it and the person who put it on a stranger
challenge.explanation: The verse includes both the person who made oil like it and the person who put it on a stranger.

questions.question: What can we infer from “holy to me throughout your generations” together with “it shall be holy unto you”?
answers: The oil’s holiness was lasting, and it belonged to the LORD throughout the generations
Anyone could make it whenever convenient
It was intended only for the generation that left Egypt
questions.explanation: Together these statements show that the oil was holy and remained associated with the LORD in future generations.

questions.question: What does “Upon man’s flesh shall it not be poured” add to the prohibition against putting it on a stranger?
answers: It was permitted only for cooking
It could not be used for ordinary personal purposes or on someone unauthorized
It could be applied to every Israelite
questions.explanation: The verse rules out ordinary use on a person’s body and specifically forbids putting it on a stranger.

questions.question: Who received the punishment of being cut off?
answers: Only the person who received the oil
Only the person who stored the oil
Both the person who compounded it and the person who put it on a stranger
questions.explanation: The verse includes both the person who made oil like it and the person who put it on a stranger.

easy.question: What did the LORD command Moses to take?
answers: Spices
Stones
Clothing
easy.explanation: The LORD commanded Moses to take spices for making the incense.

easy.question: What was to be made from the spices?
answers: Oil
Incense
Bread
easy.explanation: The passage says to make them into a perfume or incense.

easy.question: How is the incense described at the end of verse 35?
answers: Sweet and new
Large and strong
Pure and holy
easy.explanation: The incense is described as pure and holy.

medium.question: What does the instruction “of each shall there be a like weight” indicate about the spices?
answers: They were to be used in equal amounts
Only one ingredient was to be used
They were to be added at different times
medium.explanation: The instruction says that each spice was to be measured in an equal weight.

medium.question: What does “a confection after the art of the apothecary” indicate?
answers: The spices were burned immediately
They were prepared as a carefully blended aromatic mixture
The vessels were cleaned
medium.explanation: The phrase describes skilled preparation of the spices as a blended aromatic compound.

medium.question: What sequence of actions is described?
answers: Burning, gathering, and purifying
Purifying, weighing, and gathering
Taking the spices, making incense, and blending it skillfully
medium.explanation: The passage first lists the spices, then commands that they be made into incense and blended as a skilled perfumer would.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the transition from verse 34 to verse 35?
answers: The incense was not merely a list of spices but a specially prepared mixture
The spices did not need to be prepared
The spices were intended as food
challenge.explanation: Verse 34 lists the ingredients, while verse 35 describes their careful processing into a blended incense.

challenge.question: What does the description “pure and holy” teach about the incense?
answers: It was intended for household use
It was properly prepared and had a holy status
It was made from only one ingredient
challenge.explanation: The words describe both the quality of its preparation and its sacred status.

challenge.question: What does “after the art of the apothecary” emphasize?
answers: The incense was made without order
The incense was obtained ready-made from elsewhere
Preparing it required skill and professional blending
challenge.explanation: The phrase compares its preparation with the work of a skilled perfumer and emphasizes careful craftsmanship.

questions.question: What can we infer from the transition from verse 34 to verse 35?
answers: The incense was not merely a list of spices but a specially prepared mixture
The spices did not need to be prepared
The spices were intended as food
questions.explanation: Verse 34 lists the ingredients, while verse 35 describes their careful processing into a blended incense.

questions.question: What does the description “pure and holy” teach about the incense?
answers: It was intended for household use
It was properly prepared and had a holy status
It was made from only one ingredient
questions.explanation: The words describe both the quality of its preparation and its sacred status.

questions.question: What does “after the art of the apothecary” emphasize?
answers: The incense was made without order
The incense was obtained ready-made from elsewhere
Preparing it required skill and professional blending
questions.explanation: The phrase compares its preparation with the work of a skilled perfumer and emphasizes careful craftsmanship.

easy.question: What was to be done to the incense?
answers: It was to be beaten very small
It was to be painted
It was to be kept in the ark
easy.explanation: The verse says, “thou shalt beat some of it very small.”

easy.question: Where was the incense to be placed?
answers: On the outer altar
Before the testimony in the tabernacle
Outside the camp
easy.explanation: The verse says to put it before the testimony in the tabernacle.

easy.question: How does the verse describe it after it was prepared?
answers: As an ordinary substance
As a gift for a king
As most holy
easy.explanation: The verse says it would be “most holy.”

medium.question: What was to be done after the incense was beaten very small?
answers: Some of it was placed before the testimony
It was burned outside the camp
It was mixed with water
medium.explanation: The sequence is to beat it very small and then place some of it before the testimony.

medium.question: What does “where I will meet with thee” indicate about the tabernacle?
answers: It was only a storage place
It was a place where the LORD met with Moses
It was where the priests lived
medium.explanation: The words identify the tabernacle as the place where the LORD would meet with Moses.

medium.question: What does “very small” indicate about preparing the incense?
answers: It was done quickly
It was done secretly
It was crushed until very fine
medium.explanation: The instruction means that the incense was to be crushed into a very fine substance.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the instruction to beat the incense “very small”?
answers: Thorough preparation was required, not merely breaking it apart
The incense could not be touched
It was intended for one-time use only
challenge.explanation: The emphasis on making it very small shows that it had to be prepared carefully and thoroughly.

challenge.question: What is the central meaning of “most holy” in this verse?
answers: The incense was intended for sale
The incense was regarded as supremely holy
The incense was ordinary food
challenge.explanation: “Most holy” expresses the highest degree of holiness and highlights the incense’s special status.

challenge.question: What sequence of ideas appears in the verse?
answers: Holiness, crushing, and then placement
Placement, holiness, and then crushing
Crushing, placement in the appointed place, and then emphasis on holiness
challenge.explanation: The verse begins with crushing, continues with placing it before the testimony, and ends by calling it most holy.

questions.question: What can we infer from the instruction to beat the incense “very small”?
answers: Thorough preparation was required, not merely breaking it apart
The incense could not be touched
It was intended for one-time use only
questions.explanation: The emphasis on making it very small shows that it had to be prepared carefully and thoroughly.

questions.question: What is the central meaning of “most holy” in this verse?
answers: The incense was intended for sale
The incense was regarded as supremely holy
The incense was ordinary food
questions.explanation: “Most holy” expresses the highest degree of holiness and highlights the incense’s special status.

questions.question: What sequence of ideas appears in the verse?
answers: Holiness, crushing, and then placement
Placement, holiness, and then crushing
Crushing, placement in the appointed place, and then emphasis on holiness

paragraphs.title: The Prohibition Against Private Use of the Incense

easy.question: To whom was the incense holy?
answers: The king
The LORD
All the people
easy.explanation: The verse says, “it shall be unto thee holy for the LORD.”

easy.question: What was forbidden to do with the incense?
answers: Make it for personal use
Smell it in the sanctuary
Keep it in a container
easy.explanation: The verse says not to make it for yourselves, meaning it could not be prepared for personal use.

easy.question: What was the punishment for anyone who made similar incense to smell?
answers: He was fined
He was merely removed from the sanctuary
He was cut off from his people
easy.explanation: The verse says that such a person would be cut off from his people.

medium.question: Why was it forbidden to make the incense for private use?
answers: Because it was very expensive
Because it was holy to the LORD
Because no fragrance could be smelled
medium.explanation: The verse connects the prohibition on private use with the incense’s holiness to the LORD.

medium.question: What does “according to the composition thereof” refer to?
answers: The place where it was kept
The time when it was burned
Its particular formula or recipe
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the special formula used to make the sacred incense.

medium.question: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in the verses?
answers: Anyone who made similar incense for private use would be cut off from his people
Anyone who smelled the incense would receive a position
Anyone who failed to make incense would be punished immediately
medium.explanation: The passage describes making similar incense for personal enjoyment and then states the punishment of being cut off.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that the incense was called holy yet could not be made for private use?
answers: It could be used at home if carefully preserved
Its holiness required that it be kept separate from ordinary use
It was intended only to provide a pleasant smell
challenge.explanation: The verses emphasize that the incense was not an ordinary perfume but a sacred substance that could not be copied for personal use.

challenge.question: What does “to smell thereto” emphasize about the forbidden act?
answers: The prohibition concerned using the incense as personal perfume
The prohibition applied only if the incense was burned
The prohibition concerned only selling the incense
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the person made similar incense in order to enjoy its fragrance personally.

challenge.question: What is the order of ideas in these verses?
answers: The punishment is stated first, followed by the reason for the prohibition
The incense is first permitted for private use and then made holy
The incense is first declared holy and private use is forbidden, followed by the punishment
challenge.explanation: Verse 37 establishes the incense’s holiness and forbids private imitation; verse 38 gives the punishment for violating the command.
